feature: op6893 DPMAIF downlink: the modem fault is the PIT-update notification, not the ring

root_cause.what: dl_start() wrote the modem PIT-update notification even though no AP PIT entry had been added: UL_RESERVE_AO_RW (PD_UL+0xac) = 0xff followed by PD_MD_MISC+0x1c = bit 0
root_cause.why_it_is_wrong: the same-board driver sends those two writes only from drv2_dl_add_apit_num(), the path that actually adds AP entries to a running ring. Its startup path ccci_drv2_rxq_hw_int_apit() -> drv2_dl_set_apit_idx() writes only PIT_INIT_CON3 (the AP index) and UL_RESERVE_RW (index | MD_DUMMYPIT_EN)
root_cause.effect: the modem is told an index update happened when nothing changed, and its handler faults

isolation.method: the notification was split out of ring startup into its own sysfs operation, so one image can run both phases
isolation.phase_a: arm the downlink ring only, send no notification, wait 120s: no exception, ring stays armed, modem stays at HS2 with an active PDP context
isolation.phase_b: send the notification on the already armed ring: fatal within 60s
isolation.phase_b_record: ex_type=49 class=fatal pc=0x91831724 lr=0x91831764 cause=0x40800824 status=0x6002 code=0x305,0x88880302,0xcccccccc addr=0x9294f00e
isolation.conclusion: arming the ring is safe; the notification is the trigger

buffer_address_is_not_involved.measurement: after the downlink buffers were moved from one flat pool to one dma_pool buffer per BAT entry, ring_dma=0x41600000 and buf_dma=0x41601000, yet the fault address stayed at 0xb294f00f, the same value seen with the old allocation
buffer_address_is_not_involved.meaning: the fault address does not derive from the buffers the driver publishes, so the earlier hypothesis that the modem cannot reach them is not supported

both_rings_now_coexist.test: downlink armed (no notification) plus uplink started on the mapped queue, five frames sent (two IPv4 echo requests, three DNS queries), all consumed: sent=5 done=5 irqs=5 err=0 last_status=0x1
both_rings_now_coexist.consequence: the one-ring-at-a-time rule was based on the notification bug and has been removed, together with the both_rings override

still_no_downlink.measurement: with both rings healthy and a live PDP context, pit_rd stayed at 1024, irqs=0, pkts=0 over 90s after the uplink frames were consumed
still_no_downlink.note: a DNS query normally produces a reply, so the absence is evidence that either the modem does not forward these uplink frames or the downlink ring cannot deliver yet; the transport-level completion alone does not distinguish the two

allocation_change.what: the downlink packet buffers are now one dma_pool buffer per BAT entry instead of one flat coherent pool
allocation_change.why: a pool sized for the same-board geometry is a multi-megabyte contiguous allocation, which this platform refuses with -ENOMEM at 6.8 MB and 13.6 MB, so the vendor 8192-entry geometry could not be tested at all
allocation_change.status: in place; the vendor geometry has not been exercised yet because the fault was found first

not_proven: whether the modem forwards the uplink frames at all
why no downlink PIT entry is ever written, now that the ring can be armed safely
the meaning of code1=0x305 and of the fault address low half 0xf00e/0xf00f, which recurs across runs
